# INV-0002: Why did calls go up 30% in October when sales stayed the same?

## Question
Calls to the call center went from 2,400 in September to 3,120 in October. Sales stayed the same. Why?

## Answer

The extra calls were customers asking about a bill. A billing mistake on October 3 charged some customers twice. About the same number of people called to buy, so sales stayed the same.

2 of 9 sources checked by a person. 1 checked by AI, 6 not checked.

Answer marked: A person checked this

Findings behind the answer: C-002 (Not checked); C-003 (A person checked this)

Findings against the answer: C-001 (Sources disagree)

Answer reviewed: 2026-11-01 16:55 UTC

What was checked: Read the billing team's notice and the call log by reason, and spoke to the billing team lead. Sources disagree about waiting time (C-001). H-004 is not tested yet.

Why: The billing team's notice (E-007), the call log (E-006) and the billing team lead (E-009) agree. Whether those customers buy less later (H-004) is not tested yet.

## Findings

- **C-001** Callers waited too long and hung up before buying. (Sources disagree)

  - Why: This is the sales manager's view. It has not been compared with the phone system report.

  - Supported by E-002: Sales manager: we were two people short in October (Not checked)

  - Contradicted by E-003: The average wait was 40 seconds in September and 40 seconds in October (Not checked)

- **C-002** About the same number of people called to buy. (Not checked)

  - Why: The call log and the sales report agree.

  - Supported by E-001: Calls to buy: 2,000 in September, 2,050 in October. Sales: $510k in September, $512k in October (AI checked the source)

  - Supported by E-006: Calls about a bill: 400 in September, 1,070 in October (Not checked)

- **C-003** A billing mistake on October 3 charged some customers twice. (A person checked this)

  - Why: The billing team's notice and the call notes say the same thing. The extra calls start on October 3.

  - Supported by E-006: Calls about a bill: 400 in September, 1,070 in October (Not checked)

  - Supported by E-007: Notice dated October 4: 1,900 customers were charged twice on October 3 (A person checked this)

  - Supported by E-008: Call notes: 9 in 10 October calls about a bill mention being charged twice (Not checked)

  - Supported by E-009: Billing team lead: the mistake was fixed on October 5 (A person checked this)

## Still being tested

- **H-003** Something went wrong with billing in early October. (Supported; Not checked)

  - Supported by E-006: Calls about a bill: 400 in September, 1,070 in October (Not checked)

- **H-004** Customers who were charged twice are less likely to buy again. (Not tested yet; Not checked)

## Ruled out

- **H-001** A new ad brought in more callers. (Ruled out; Not checked)

  - Contradicted by E-004: No new ads ran in October (Not checked)

- **H-002** We raised prices, so callers did not buy. (Ruled out; Not checked)

  - Contradicted by E-005: Prices were the same in September and October (Not checked)

## Follow-up questions

- **Q-003** Have all 1,900 customers been paid back? (Open)

- **Q-004** Should we expect fewer sales in November from the customers who were charged twice? (Deferred)

  - Deferred: Waiting for the November sales report on December 1.

## Sources

- **E-001** Calls to buy: 2,000 in September, 2,050 in October. Sales: $510k in September, $512k in October (Call log and October sales report: Call log, September and October; October sales report; AI checked the source)

  - The call log counts 2,000 calls to buy in September and 2,050 in October. The October sales report shows $510k of sales in September and $512k in October.

- **E-002** Sales manager: we were two people short in October (Sales manager, in the Monday sales meeting; Not checked)

  - The sales manager said in the Monday sales meeting that the call center was two people short in October. She thinks callers waited too long and hung up before buying.

- **E-003** The average wait was 40 seconds in September and 40 seconds in October (Phone system report: Phone system report, September and October; Not checked)

  - The phone system report shows callers waited 40 seconds on average in September and 40 seconds in October. 3% of callers hung up while waiting in both months.

- **E-004** No new ads ran in October (Marketing calendar: Marketing calendar, September and October; Not checked)

  - The marketing calendar lists the same two ads in September and October. Nothing new started in October.

- **E-005** Prices were the same in September and October (Price list: Price list, last changed July 1; Not checked)

  - The price list has not changed since July 1.

- **E-006** Calls about a bill: 400 in September, 1,070 in October (Call log: Call log, September and October, by reason; Not checked)

  - The call log gives a reason for every call. Calls about a bill went from 400 in September to 1,070 in October. Calls to buy went from 2,000 to 2,050. The extra bill calls start on October 3.

- **E-007** Notice dated October 4: 1,900 customers were charged twice on October 3 (Email from the billing team: Email to all staff, October 4, subject: Customers charged twice on October 3; A person checked this)

  - The billing team emailed all staff on October 4. A mistake in the October 3 billing run charged 1,900 customers twice. The team said refunds would go out within a week.

- **E-008** Call notes: 9 in 10 October calls about a bill mention being charged twice (Call log notes: Call log, October, notes column; Not checked)

  - Of the 1,070 calls about a bill in October, 960 have a note that says the customer was charged twice. In September none did.

- **E-009** Billing team lead: the mistake was fixed on October 5 (Billing team lead, in person; A person checked this)

  - The billing team lead said in person that the October 3 billing run charged 1,900 customers twice, and that the mistake was fixed on October 5.
